gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.

gaps.sentence: They don't allow ___ in the museum.
gaps.hint: allow + noun / allow sb to do
gaps.explanation: allow + noun/-ing (no personal object): they don't allow photography. With a person: allow visitors to photograph.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford ___ another month abroad.
She avoided ___ about the incident for weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Avoid' is always followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: He's considering ___ his job and travelling for a year.
He denied ___ the money, but nobody believed him.
